Welcome to the first of hopefully many CHALLENGE posts. Alright my friends, these prompts are to be used for practice- like exercises for your brain. There will be guidelines for each new challenge that are prompt specific, but there are also a few general rules (that some of you might hate me for):

GENERAL RULES

-Content should be new and original. No fanfiction (unless the prompt DIRECTLY calls for it)

-No posting what you've already written (if you absolutely MUST use previously written stuff, write CHEATMODE on your submission)

-Remember, this is for practice. Don't worry if your submission isn't prefect. Positive feedback will be on the way

-To request blunt feedback (such as you want us to be impartial ) just write "Blunt Feedback Please"

THE PROMPT

*Genre : Fantasy *type : Setting

You are now the creator of a fantasy world. For this prompt, you must create a location in your world and the inhabitants

Do:

Write a setting in a fantasy world. Be as specific as possible. You must create one specific location, describe it and name it. Describe the race and culture of the inhabitants of your location. The only characters allowed are those related to culture/history of your inhabitants. Historical events are allowed.

E.G.: You create a woodland based kingdom named Tallulah. The citizens are elves. You must go into depth as to why this isn't a LotR rip off.

Do Not

Write dialogues, create specific characters that aren't pertinent to history/culture, Do not present any plot that is not related to history/culture.

Alright guys, have fun and good luck. I look forward to reading your histories and about your new civilizations! I'll be participating as well!

Anthropological Survey of Tawa and the Culture surrounding the Angali

The view from the ground is astonishing. As one looks up onto the horizon, at the very peak of the highest mountain, a small glimmer in the setting sun can be seen. Peering through a glass, one can see the gold and red shimmers of large structures perched on top of and on the side of the mountain’s face. Trees surrounding the base, one can almost miss the ornately carved stairs, covered by dirt and foliage. a large serpent made of stone, metal, and jewels guards the steps. Decorated in golden scales, some picked away by scavengers looking to make away with loot, two large green glass eyes stare down at the travellers who dare approach the gate. Judging by the height of the mountain, one can assume that ascending will take four days time.

On the ascent, looking around, one can notice carved figures of animals. A jaguar, a monkey, humanoid figures, and symbols that seem to indicate directions. Each decorated in colorful paint and stones, though some of the stones were looted by unworthy travellers.

Drawing closer to the top, one notices golden feathers inlays on the stony steps. There is a wall. Opening the gate is a risky business. Those who survive the climb might not survive the greeting. The customary way to enter the city is to light a flame in a small basin near the feet of a large hawk statue. If deemed worthy, the traveller can enter.

Entering the city is something to behold. The first stop in the gate is the peak, as the sides are walled off. A pristine lake sits atop the mountain, surrounded by glowing flora and strange fauna. One will note it is not considered good manners to step into the lake without the proper cleansing ritual. Sitting in the middle of the lake, is another large hawk statue. Her wings outstretched, one can estimate a 12 meter wingspan. Her eyes carved from amber, they look toward the West, reflecting the fiery light of the sun.

The architecture is a mix of erected buildings, toward the center of the city, and carved buildings, toward the outskirts. The peoples there, The Anagli, Children of Tawa, are humanoid in figure. They too have wings, their feathers in assorted colors. The Angali, a curious group of citizens, will stare at outsiders openly. The younger of the Angali might approach a traveller with small, glowing flowers they call “moonflowers.” The elders will then take the traveller to their council building -- a floating island atop the Lake.

During this period, one can expect to sit alone while the Elders ask Tawa, their goddess. After they return, the traveller must don the ceremonial dress. It is a long, red robe with golden stitch to mimic feathers.

The reason for this is to mimic Tawa’s feathers. One must become close to Tawa to understand the winged Angali.

Excerpt from the Angali Lore, Book of Tawa:

In the land's beginning, the Great Spirits flew freely. Wada, the first spirit, had many children. Wada is the energy that began the pristine lands and lakes. Wada's eldest child, the large Serpant Inad, guarded the land. His scales were gold and turquoise, his eyes make from the volcanic glass from the mountain where he was born. From the heavy fog of the sea, Wada created the large sea snake, Ayami. Ayami guarded the waters, his scales silver and grey from the waters where he was born. Wada then created Tawa and Aka, The twin sisters of the sky. Tawa, golden and light in color, quickly gained the favor of Inad, who vowed to protect her. Aka, dark in color, her feathers dull, grew jealous of Inad's brotherly affection for Tawa. While Tawa and Inad grew and played together, basking in the setting sun, Aka sat in darkness. Many years passed, and Aka abandoned Tawa, choosing to go to the easternmost tip of the world to begin her new life. Tawa, kind in nature, wished her luck.

Tawa, despite having her brother Inad to speak with, grew lonely. She desired her own family, to love and protect. She then flew to the sun, and asked Wada for a gift. Wada, sensing her sorrow, and her kind spirit, agreed to the request. Wada forced the sun's sparkling rays to stretch down toward the golden Tawa, enveloping her in light. She stretched her large wings open, and was impregnated by the sun.

Our Mother Tawa birthed a single large egg in her nest atop the small hill of Anga. The large, golden egg sat for 300 years, awaiting the time to hatch. Tawa cared for it every day, keeping it warm and loved. Her children would soon be welcomed to the world. Inad left her, hesitantly, wandering to find a safer spot for Tawa's children. It was then that Aka decided to return.

Jealous once again of Tawa’s love of the unhatched children, Aka set out to destroy her sister. Aka had a black, scale covered egg of her own that had hatched many years prior. She did not love it as Tawa loved her egg. The creatures birthed by her were consumed with darkness. Aka’s children were the first instance of evil in the world. Tawa’s the first of light.

Aka wanted to attack the golden egg, the life that emerged would surely kill that which she mothered. Calling her unholy children, Aka set toward Anga hill, her children following. The setting sun gleamed against the golden egg as the first crack emerged on its handsome shell. Light emitted, but darkness came.

Tawa, sensing trouble, prepared for the battle, which lasted many suns and moons. The cracks in the egg became more prominent as Aka’s attack continued. Tawa, the holiest of spirits, fought, protecting her precious children as Aka’s drew closer. When the egg finally hatched, Tawa’s children emerged. Warriors, like herself, but unwise and unprotected. Some of the children perished, their wings broken in Aka’s beak. Aka took Tawa and threw her to the ground, breaking the earth, creating a hole.

Tawa screeched to the sky. The scream could be heard throughout the land. Ayami heard the call first, and set out to find Inad. Inad rushed back, Tawa's screams still filling the sky and rupturing the great mountains, forcing water to spill, creating the first waterfalls. Inad, the large serpent, finally returned. He saw Aka clashing her black talons into Tawa, her new children fearing for their lives. Inad reared up from the depths below and took Aka by her bosom and dragged her to the underworld. And Tawa’s children prevailed.

She fell down into the massive crater, another screech emitting from her golden beak. The ground shook, and Angal grew into a mountain, the flat basin on top, and a single crater. Her children surrounded her.

“Do not fear my children, you will grow, and you all carry within you my light. Look to the west, The sun will guide you.” She told them. She closed her eyes, and her children wept. Their tears filled the basin, but from her death, sprung life. And Now, the Children of Tawa, remain in her debt.

Inad returned, only to find a mountain that he could not climb. Hoping they would be protected, he curled up at the base and vowed to protect the children of his beloved sister, whom he, in his own mind, had failed.

The Angali are a spiritual group, Tawa their mother, their Protector is Inad. They look to the west for inspiration. They are not intolerant, and often leave the golden walls of Tawa. Their sense of the earth below them remains strong. If one exudes light, they will accept the person in question, if not, they might attack. For this, the Angali are feared. But they do not qualm over this, their slight bodies are capable of fighting, and their amber eyes watch all.

Continuation of the Study of Tawa and the Angali

As one might assume, the tomes of lore in the majestic floating library atop Lake Tawa are magnificent in volume. The scrolling, curled text can take years to master, but well worth the study. The Angali do not like Aka nor her children, and as such her story is not mentioned in The Book of Tawa for fear that darkness will creep into the city and taint the light of Angal.

Instead, one will find a single tome of Aka. To read this tome, however, one must ask permission from the elders and undergo a ceremonial cleansing. This will take days, if not weeks. However, to truly understand the Angali and their enemies, the trek is well worth it.

The ceremonial cleanse begins with a day long fast, beginning at sunrise. The traveller will sit at the base of the statue of Tawa, alone and unclothed. This process is believed to let the sun’s light purify the seeker of knowledge and induce one into the tribe. In the sun’s final journey to the west, the seeker is then presented a flower. The flower, turquoise in hue, glows strangely in the darkening sky. An elder leads the seeker to the gate of the golden city and accompanies the seeker on the journey down. The elder carries the Book of Aka in a special cloth, rumored to be woven from strands of moonflower that grew in the sunlight.

The flower does not die, despite being separated from the roots. Instead, it acts as the light needed in the darkness. The journey down is perhaps more arduous than the ascent, but necessary for knowledge and truth.

At the base, the seeker must face the golden statue of Inad. The elder outstretches his hands, closes his eyes, and hands the seeker a knife. Making a small incision on the seeker’s left hand, the blood collected is then placed in the serpent’s mouth.

The ground will shake. Behind the statue, a cave opens up, and the elder urges the seeker in. Standing outside, the Elder waits.

The seeker is then greeted by a low rumbling noise, resonating through the body. It is very important the flower does not touch the ground. As instructed, the seeker must hold out the flower as a cold wind surrounds them, and a heavy, scaled creature wraps its body around you.

This is Inad, the Protector. He is more beautiful than the lore described. Alternating patterns of gold and turquoise scales cover his long, heavy body. Around what one would describe as a neck, a piece of rope with a single, large gold feather dangles. He will sniff the flower, uncoil from around you, and rear his magnificent head. His glass eyes stare deeply into the seeker’s. His tongue flicks out and in repeatedly. He will ask the seeker a single question.

“What is it you seek?” to which the seeker responds, simply, “Truth.” If deemed worthy, he calls the elder in, who will bow. If deemed unworthy, the seeker’s body will be consumed.

“An unholy tome of the beast that attempted to destroy light. You have my permission to gaze upon the contents.”

The contents, short and unromantic, spin a story of darkness.

Book of Aka

Aka, hatred filling her soul, left Tawa, Inad, and Ayami. Her tattered feathers carried her to the easternmost point of the world. Wada did not like this. Wada could no longer see Aka.

She perched in a cave atop the mountain of Yanik. Yanik, an old spirit, just as Wada, grew in shadows. With no physical form, Yanik is where there is darkness.

There she brooded for eighty days, her mind focused on the jealousy of the golden Tawa. Her tattered feathers ruffled, as the world around her faded out. Yanik approached the young Aka. Yanik offered her a way to defeat the Golden Tawa, through form of children, as he would sire them.

Agreeing, Aka allowed darkness to penetrate her, the seed of evil planted. She birthed a single, large, black egg. But she did not love it. It was a tool. Her children, conceived in hatred, would never grow to know love like the Angali know love.

Her children hatched, their grey skin ashen, their feathers matted. She would use them to attack all hope Tawa would have.

The tome concluded. Simply a few short paragraphs. One can ascend the mountains again. Inad curled up in his lonely cave.

In the land of Aeros exists the great race of the Torva, they are a strange breed though, massively different from the others. They have bodies that feel cold and hard as rock, yet their movements are not stiff, they are fluid, graceful even. They don't really have skin, their entire composition is uniform, they are as living rock, they crack and shatter when struck, and their dead look like statues. They can completely regenerate themselves from their core-stones, which look like fist sized chunks of obsidian that reside within the centre of their torsos.

They vary in colour, from a pale blue from the ones that live in the west, to a blood red from the north east, in the central parts of their lands most are grey or green, with a similar texture to granite. The colour they are is regarded similar to how hair colour is regarded for us, it's a minor difference, and often ignored when judging someone. There is nearly no racism among the Torva.

They have an interesting power though, they call it weighting, it's the ability to increase the density of any part of their bodies. The clear violation of conservation of mass is explained by the innate magic that resides within them, it's the same magic that animates them, letting solid rock live and move. The power of weighting only applies to their own body, and cannot stretch beyond that.

Much like how we have arm wrestles the Torva have a challenge called fist crushing, each player places their fists in front of them, their left over the opponents right. When a signal is given they use weighting to try and crush the opponents fist with their left hand, while at the same time increasing the density of their right hand to avoid it being crushed. It's usually played till one player surrenders, they feel pain as the pressure increases, though some might keep going till they crack. In most tournament games it carries on until one of them has their fist shatter.

This however is nothing compared to the fighting pits. A 1 vs 1 spar in a smallish circular arena, the arena has a pit around the side, to surrender you simply have to jump off, the fall isn't far. knocking people out of the arena also counts, as well as shattering them. The most skilled Torva at the art of weighting can increase the density of their arm from it having a mass of a few hundred grams while they launch it towards their opponent, to it weighing more than 10 tonnes as it makes contact. The opponent however can weight the impact site and soak the damage with only a few cracks at most if they see it coming in time.

The fighters have a choice when fighting as to how light they want to be, some keep themselves at as little as 20kg, when a full grown Torva usually hits over 300kg. Making yourself light increases your mobility, but it also makes you more vulnerable, a single hit with no preparation and the fight is over for you. Making yourself denser though can be equally problematic, the Torva are stronger than any human, but their strength still has a limit, so though you can take more hits, moving around eats away at your stamina and the enemy can simply tire you out of a fight.

The Torva are a mostly peaceful race, but many times people have mistaken an unwillingness to fight for an inability to fight. The Thaumers, whose lands lie on the same continent as the Torva even have the short and sweet proverb 'Only a fool declares war on rocks'. They call their old king the mad king for trying to invade Torva lands so often, he lost every battle and eventually his military was too weak to hold back the uprising the came to dethrone him. Other races have tried too, sending ships over to try and get a foot in the door of the eastern continent, each one of them has had a swift and crushing defeat except for the brotherhood of black blood, a group of humans that could face them toe to toe using their incredibly specialized magic.

The Political system of the Torva is a technocracy, the most skilled in each area oversee it, with a parliament of the greatest and wisest of the Torva ruling over the rest. They copied the system off the Thaumers, both races had a monarchy before the mad king was overthrown, but after the Thaumers created a technocratic society, and their prosperity grew enormously, the monarchy of the Torva voluntarily stepped down from ruling the land so that they could adopt the system too, though they did continue to be a respected presence in Torvan culture.

The Torvan speak in Torvic, a language that outsiders would describe as 'churning gravel, the roar of a landslide and the rumble of thunder, all at once'. The language is impossible to understand or imitate by the other races without some very impressive communication magics. They can also speak the common tongue, though it's differences to their language make it difficult. Their language system speaks all the meanings of a sentence at once, with even more layers on top to help you decode it, it's incredibly efficient for information transferal, with entire sentences taking a couple of seconds to say. The idea of saying information in a single string is alien to them, hence their difficulty with the common tongue.

Torvic does however have a disadvantage, they have no written language. They can draw out rudimentary symbols and art which offers some solid media, but otherwise their collective knowledge is not recorded, merely passed down though the Torva from the old to the young, they also have memories that put the other races to shame, this coupled with their 400 year life expectancy means that their knowledge is rarely lost.

The Torva never hold grudges, their culture judges people based on their current state, their current motives etc. This is why even after declaring war and having multiple battles the Torva consider themselves allies to the rest of the world, especially the Thaumers who shared their politics and technology with the Torva in return for their immense knowledge, though the language barrier between them sometimes limits what can be shared either way.

I would be happy to explain some of the other races in detail, I have decided that there are 6 in total, 4 live on the great continent (Humans, Fae, Lereshi and Kautl), and 2 on the eastern (Torva and Thaumers).

The scrying window was opened for the 2054th time this morn. It opened the same as the last 1045 times, without indecent. No magical cascade, no causalities, no bleed through. The only thing of note this time was what the window showed us. This time, there where creatures, creatures with minds that may be like our own.

The window opened up to a meadow, surrounded by a thin forest. This is again the world of Alesixia {See Index Scroll 1452 for list of Alesixia scrolls} as showed by the light red skies and dual suns risings from the horizon. The trees are of the same type as to be expected from this world, thin trunks with large, wide leaves. Their bark looks to be thin and pale, ranging from thin grey to light brown. The leaves a dark green, presumably to draw sunlight. The grass in the meadow is of the short, light variation. It becomes a no darker green, than the light bark of the trees.

A scribe noted the bird like insects resting in the trees. They tend to favor the higher branches, for reasons unknown. Scribe Tallius surmised it may have something to do with the intense sunlight, but it isn't a pressing matter. We need to see a specimen closer than we have before they become important. This viewing was able to reaffirm that these creatures are similar to the insects of our world, but much larger than ours. They are shaped like our birds, a carapace in the center, and wings set out to the side. There seem to be no casing for their wings, one will just tuck them to it's sides when not it use. This is the behavior that first led to their approximation to birds. No new colors where seen, still only ranging from dark to bright red. When the 'flock' flew out of the trees, they may have been lead by the brightest colored, but it was difficult to see from the angle of this window. It may be possible that there is a correlation between color and leadership, this has been noted and will be investigated at later viewing.

Nothing else of interest was noted for rest of the day. As the window was being prepared for closure, Scribe Tallius stopped me. He believed he saw something large moving in the tree line. The window was left open for temporary investigation. There was indeed something moving, quickly covering ground towards the window. The creature was tall and thin, as it hid easily behind the thin trees and it's head was among the lower branches. It would duck to move from tree to tree, but then stand fully when it wasn't moving. It reached the closest tree to the window, only the length of two men away. That's when the impossible happened.

The creature stepped out from behind the tree, then walked in front of the window.

It looked at us. It looked at us from the other side of the scrying window. Tallius dropped his scrolls, the creature ran at the loud noise.

We elected to leave the window open over the night. Scribes where posted, but nothing else was reported.

{Scroll 266 - 47th day of our God Telon's phase, 589th year of the 5th Age}

The Headmaster has been notified, we have been instructed to leave the window open until we know more of what is happening. This is the first time any creature, of any world has been able to see the scrying mirror. This is unheard of, even in our own world. The other side of the mirror cannot be seen by mortal's eyes. The only reason we can see the side of the mirror located in the academy is because it is bound by powerful, ancient magic.

More creatures arrived to the meadow today. None of them have come close to the mirror, they have all stayed well within the tree line. It was hard to count, but there could have been no more than ten.

It was elected to leave the window open again on this night.

{Scroll 315 - 2nd day of our God Faathu's phase, 589th year of the 5th Age}

Much has happened in these past days, I will surmise them in this scroll. Full notes are held within scrolls numbered 267-310.

On the 48th morning of Telon's phase, the creatures started gathering in numbers. It started slowly, only one or two at time. Around midday they came in larger numbers, until by that afternoon they were uncountable. They filled the meadow and the trees around it. There were easily more than the King's Guard here at the academy, they number 50 or more at their lowest.

These creatures are tall, a head and a half taller than any man alive, they are thinner than a man as well, at least by half. The skin color had variations of a light red, but not much. There were none darker than the color of blood, and none lighter than a rose. Each had 2 legs, and 4 arms, each with two joints, one at the torso and a knee or elbow like in the middle of the limb. Both arms and legs ended in the same appendage. Six digits, four fingers and two thumbs. Each digit is longer than a mans, it is believed that they have an extra joint in each, for a total 4, Their fingers are thin and precise, but by no means delicate.

Their whole bodies are taunt and lean. Muscles are easily seen, and they move with a gracefulness I've only seen in cats and dancers. They adorn themselves not in clothing, but trinkets I would expect to see on barbarians. Furs, bones, wooden panels, and the like. Some wear nothing more than fur collars, other have covered their whole torso. These seem to be linked to a hierarchy, but we are still unsure.

The creatures gathered, but that was all. They seemed to be waiting for something. On the next morn, that something came. Some time after the crowd parted and what looked like a tribal chieftain was lead to the window. It sat down in front of the window and closed it's eyes. Their head are the most dissimilar to men. Smooth, lacking many features, no hair, ears, or lips. Their mouths are a hard ribbed beak that grows where a man' teeth would be. The features, or lack there of are very unsettling. Nothing happened for many hours.

As the sun set, the creature that is presumed to be a leader opened it's eyes. Then it's mouth. And with a loud boom, it spoke.

My ears did not understand the words that it spoke, but my mind did. I do not know who it could communicate with us through the window, even we are unable to do that. It's voice was loud within everyone's minds, and to painful for most. Everyone but Tallius and I left, we stayed with our scrolls. He told us his people's story.

We are the Annukta

Our people travel many lands

Under many suns

Annukta are old as the magic that hold worlds together

Annukta were born of the Old Gods

Annukta are Gods

We travel in the space between worlds

We travel and eat

We carry pieces of worlds with us

We carry what we eat

But we are trapped

Trapped on this world

These suns would not let us leave

So we wait, and become hungry

Then you open door to this world

We are trapped no more

And soon hungry no more

The scrying window closed, and with it the voice inside of our heads. Some don't believe Tallius and I, but we did not close the window. In fact we have not been able to open another window since. Something has taken control away from us.

Word has been sent to the King for aid.

I fear it will be to late.
